evidence.completeLockedSourceExcerpt: actually give you the answer why do we have earthquakes why do we have tsunamis simple answer because we live in a universe that has plate tectonics they point out by the way that this that this quality of our universe plate tectonics which is movements under if you will the ocean floor and the earth floor is as far as we know astronomically unique no other planet has plate tectonics and why do we need plate tectonics is it to stabilize the climate yes is it ultimately to keep the land separate from the water yes but the ultimate reason is actually the most interesting at of all if we didn't have plate tectonics we wouldn't have life we wouldn't have human life no we wouldn't have human life or animal life or any kind of complex life whatsoever in other words our universe operates according to what can be called a fine-tuned or anthropic principle many of the properties of the universe must be what they are because if they weren't we wouldn't be here this comes back to the question I raised earlier why did God create a lawful universe why did he create in it autonomous human beings like you and me who could not only do good but also do evil I think God did that not only because this is a wonderful powerful grand awesome world that we live in but I think also because God in some senses wanted to create human beings who share his autonomy who share his free will and with the free will to do good comes also alas the free will to do evil before we condemn that system we have to ask do we have have we seriously thought about a different kind of universe that we could devise better thank you very much
evidence.assessmentRationale: Strongest feature: D’Souza offers two mechanisms, claiming in the excerpt that tectonics enables life and autonomous freedom permits goodness and evil, thereby engaging natural and moral suffering with responsiveness and relevance. Principal limitation: The necessity of tectonics for complex life receives insufficient support, while freedom does not explain suffering unrelated to choice, depressing evidentiary warrant and tempering logical coherence and calibration. Live burden: He must establish that these risks are indispensable to life and meaningful agency, then show that their value justifies the magnitude and distribution of suffering under a good creator.

anonymousReviewerPositions.rationale: The closing challenge asks whether critics can devise a better universe, but the core case also offers positive claims about tectonics and freedom. Those claims are insufficiently supported; the conclusion is not clearly treated as true solely because alternatives remain unproved.

candidates.label: Scope neglect
candidates.definition: Failing to adjust judgment in proportion to the scale, number, or magnitude of what is being discussed.
